source.title: Implicit Regularization in Over-parameterized Neural Networks
source.authors: M. Kubo; Ryotaro Banno; Hidetaka Manabe; Masataka Minoji

record.file_problem: none; supplied text includes the paper through its proofs and references.
record.tranche_reason: Measures gradient variation and output interpolation in trained ReLU networks as a distinct measure of properties associated with generalization; it does not directly measure the training-to-test error gap or the claim versions' listed interventions.
record.gate_note: Reports gradient gap deviation, gradient deflection, and pair margin/fluctuation results. Initialization-only measures and comparisons to cited prior work are not separate result rows. Its results do not directly establish that networks fitting arbitrary labels generalize on natural labels.
record.test_reason: The study measures variation of network outputs and derivatives along input interpolation paths. These are related complexity measures, not tests of V1–V8. In particular, input-gradient variation is not V7's sensitivity to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, and no generalization-gap ranking is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors interpret small gradient variation in the tested ReLU networks as near-linear interpolation between samples and propose that initialization and SGD constrain gradient gaps and node counts. Training-step comparisons use normalized outputs. Their suggested connection between pair margin/fluctuation and validation accuracy remains tentative, and the relation between these complexity measures and generalization is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Measures gradient variation along input interpolation paths and pair margin/fluctuation; does not measure the claim versions' test-error effects or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported measures depend on dataset; pair margin/fluctuation are shown for MNIST, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 with different model examples. The paper says small fluctuation depends on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At initialization, gradient gap deviation and gradient deflection are small across the tested MLP, VGG, and residual networks; the MLP measures hardly change with width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly initialized ReLU networks can have small input-gradient variation along paths between image samples despite substantial architectural capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-step experiments investigate gradient variation using normalized outputs; the authors explicitly describe small post-training variation and approximate random-walk behavior for VGG and ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD-trained ReLU networks can retain small input-gradient variation along interpolation paths between samples.

fits_no_version.finding: Pair margin exceeds pair fluctuation as training progresses in the three illustrated model–dataset combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training can raise endpoint classification margins above deviations of midpoint outputs from endpoint interpolation.

record.problems: The paper notes that the constitutive relation between generalization and implicit regularization is left for future work. Several training-step results are figure-only without numerical values in the supplied text. The experiments focus on three image datasets and reported ReLU architectures.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural and random labels.
No test-error sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance comparison under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout or weight-decay intervention measuring held-out error.

Entire version untested: no magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap correlation, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The record's tested_not_extracted designation is incorrect.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern related constructs outside V1–V8. Their cannot_determine states indicate that they cannot establish a claim-version effect, not that the reported qualitative observations are absent. No claim verdicts are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep of test error past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparison on held-out performance.

The study measures gradient gap deviation and gradient deflection, not magnitude-aware sharpness or a ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; it does not report a training-to-test gap correlation.
No example removal or retraining experiment.
